table_title: List the top 3 highest mountains per continent with height in metres, the country or countries the summit lies in, and the year of first summit.
db_analog: SELECT continent, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY continent ORDER BY height_m DESC) AS rank, mountain, height_m, countries, year_of_first_summit FROM source_defined_continent_mountain_rankings QUALIFY rank <= 5 ORDER BY continent, rank
temporal_note: Wikipedia per-continent master ranking articles + per-mountain articles, accessed 2026-04-27 to 2026-04-28. Heights and per-continent top-5 rankings come from height-ordered Wikipedia sources: List of highest mountains on Earth (Asia); Andes (South America, including Peru's Huascarán per the article's stated heights); List of mountain peaks of North America; Caucasus Mountains (Europe); List of mountains in Africa (which explicitly applies a topographic-prominence > 500 m independent-mountain rule); Sentinel Range (Antarctica, raw elevation); List of highest mountains of New Guinea (Oceania, applies a height >=3750m + prominence >=500m ranked-list rule). First-summit years come from per-mountain Wikipedia pages where they exist. Five rows have 'unknown' as the Year of First Summit because Wikipedia does not record the first ascent: Cerro Bonete (S America #5), Pushkin Peak (Europe #5), Clinch/Corbet/Schoening Peaks (Antarctica #3-#5). Per-continent independent-mountain conventions vary by source: Africa explicitly applies prominence > 500 m; Oceania applies a height >=3750m + prominence >=500m ranking rule per the List of highest mountains of New Guinea master article (which excludes Sumantri / Ngga Pulu / East Carstensz Peak as subsidiary peaks); Antarctica uses raw elevation per the Sentinel Range article. The instance commits to each continent's source convention rather than imposing a single global rule.
_extraction_notes: Derived from top_5_highest_mountains_per_continent by deterministic filter/projection on the parent CSV. Rank filter Rank <= 3.
